events.title: Negev Bedouin concentrated in the Siyag
events.summary: After the 1948 war only about 11,000 of an estimated 65,000-95,000 Negev Bedouin remained, according to Human Rights Watch. Under the military rule imposed on Arab citizens (1949-1966), authorities moved 11 of the 19 remaining tribes into the Siyag, a restricted zone mostly east and southeast of Beersheba; HRW reports the Bedouin were told the move was temporary, and that the removal was complete by 1 April 1952. Much of the land they left was later registered as state land, and Israeli historians cited by HRW say around 50 Jewish settlements were built in that area in the early 1950s.

affected_populations.note: HRW: 11 of the 19 tribes left in the Negev were moved into the Siyag; Israeli Ministry of Agriculture figures (via HRW) say two-thirds of Siyag residents in 1955 had been displaced from the western Negev. No total count of displaced persons given.
Jewish Israelis: HRW, citing Swirski and Hasson, says around 50 Jewish settlements were built in the vacated area in the early 1950s; no Israeli casualties reported.

events.title: Prawer-Begin bill on Negev Bedouin shelved
events.title_he: גניזת הצעת חוק פראוור-בגין להסדרת התיישבות הבדואים בנגב
events.summary: The Prawer-Begin bill, built on a committee's proposals to settle Bedouin land claims and including the demolition of dozens of unrecognised villages, would have moved about 40,000 Bedouin citizens into government-planned towns (Al Jazeera; The Independent put estimates at 40,000-70,000 'depending on who you ask'). The government said the plan would modernise the Bedouin and improve their quality of life, earmarking $340m, while human rights groups including Adalah and Human Rights Watch said it failed to recognise Bedouin land claims; Adalah counts some 70,000 residents of the unrecognised villages. The Knesset passed a first reading 43-40 in June 2013, and protests followed, including in Hura on 30 November. On 12 December 2013 Benny Begin announced the bill was being shelved, saying there was 'no majority in the coalition', and Netanyahu approved.

affected_populations.note: Plan would have moved ~40,000 (Al Jazeera, Guardian) or 40,000-70,000 (The Independent, citing differing estimates); shelved before implementation. Adalah counts 70,000 residents of unrecognised villages; HRW (2008) counted 39 unrecognised villages.
No Israeli casualties reported; right-wing MKs opposed the bill's offer of cash and land ownership to Bedouin (Al Jazeera).

events.summary: On 25 March 2019 President Donald Trump signed a proclamation recognising the Golan Heights as part of the State of Israel, with Prime Minister Netanyahu at the White House; the proclamation cited threats from Iran and Hezbollah in southern Syria. Israel's 1981 effective annexation had never been recognised internationally, and a 1981 UN Security Council resolution declared it 'null and void'. The UN Secretary-General's spokesman said the Golan's status had not changed, and Syria, Turkey, Qatar and the Arab League rejected the move.

events.title: Trump unveils 'Peace to Prosperity' plan
events.summary: On 28 January 2020 President Trump presented his 'Vision for Peace' at the White House alongside Netanyahu: a demilitarised Palestinian state, Jerusalem as Israel's undivided capital with a Palestinian capital including areas of East Jerusalem, and Israeli sovereignty over West Bank settlements and the Jordan Valley. Netanyahu, who had pledged in September 2019 to apply sovereignty over the Jordan Valley, agreed to negotiate on its basis, as did opposition leader Benny Gantz. Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas and Hamas rejected it; the PLO said it would leave Palestinians about 15% of 'historic Palestine'. In 'day of rage' protests the next day, the Palestinian health ministry said three Palestinians were injured by live fire near Ramallah.

affected_populations.note: Palestinian health ministry (via BBC): three injured by live fire in clashes near Ramallah on 29 Jan 2020; others hurt by rubber-coated bullets.

events.title: Iran nuclear deal (JCPOA) concluded
events.summary: On 14 July 2015 China, France, Germany, Russia, the United Kingdom, the United States, the EU High Representative and Iran concluded the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action on Iran's nuclear programme, a deal Israel's government had campaigned against. The UN Security Council unanimously endorsed it in Resolution 2231 on 20 July 2015, and Implementation Day came on 16 January 2016 after the IAEA confirmed Iran's initial nuclear steps.

events.summary: On 8 May 2018 President Trump announced the end of US participation in the JCPOA and ordered sanctions re-imposed on Iran's energy, petrochemical and financial sectors, calling the deal 'one of the worst and most one-sided transactions' the US had entered. UN sanctions on Iran were later re-applied, effective 27 September 2025, under Resolution 2231's procedure.

events.title: Cross-Israel Highway (Route 6) opens
events.summary: The Cross-Israel Highway, built and operated by private companies as the country's first toll road, opened on 4 August 2002. Work on its central section between the Sorek and Iron interchanges began in November 1999, and the 87 km central section opened in stages between 2002 and January 2004. Intended to link the periphery to the centre and disperse population, it carried about 130,000 vehicles a day by 2010.
